biography: Born in the heart of British motorsport country, Steve Soper's journey began not in a go-kart, but tinkering with his father's old Mini Cooper in the garage. The roar of engines at nearby Brands Hatch always beckoned, and by 18, he'd traded spanners for steering wheels, entering local club races with a ferocity that belied his age. Early success led to a stint in Formula Ford, but it was touring cars where Soper truly found his calling. His aggressive, no-holds-barred style quickly caught the eye of BMW Motorsport, propelling him into the world of international GT racing. Though frustratingly inconsistent in temperament, his raw speed and undeniable talent made him a sought-after commodity. Now at his peak, Soper aims to convert potential into enduring legacy.
drivingStyle: Soper is a master of controlled aggression. He attacks corners with remarkable precision, often pushing the limits of grip to gain an advantage. Tire management isn't his strongest suit; he prefers an all-out assault, relying on his raw pace to compensate. Under pressure, Soper can either rise to the occasion with a stunning display of skill, or crack spectacularly. His inconsistent temperament often dictates which way the wind blows. He is known for his daring overtaking moves and late-braking maneuvers.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, regardless of the weather.
Listens to heavy metal music at full volume right up until the moment he gets into the car.
Has a peculiar habit of talking to his steering wheel before each race, giving it a pep talk.
famousQuote: Racing isn't about playing nice. It's about leaving it all on the track, and damn the consequences.
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Spa in 1997, driving a BMW McLaren F1 GTR, after an epic battle with the factory Porsche team.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 1996 Macau Guia Race, costing him the championship and severely damaging his reputation.
